title: Commission a jacketed-reactor cascade
physicalPurpose: Reject utility disturbances in the fast jacket loop before they propagate into product temperature.
principalTechnique: Inner-first cascade commissioning and time-scale separation
objective: Commission a jacket-temperature inner loop before closing a reactor-temperature outer loop.

simplifications: Local linear energy balances around one production operating point
One ideal temperature measurement for each jacket and reactor state
Three deterministic equivalent plants isolate controller structure and inner-loop tuning
Controller requests are used as applied valve positions because no actuator nonideality is configured

baseline.limitation: Direct reactor-temperature PI cannot act until the slow product temperature has already changed.

change.decision: Accept cascade only when the inner loop is commissioned first, detects the disturbance earlier, is at least three times faster, and improves equivalent reactor-temperature evidence.

disturbances: Commissioning run steps both jacket setpoints from 70 to 75 degC at 10.0 s
Regulatory run changes utility contribution from 0 to -10 degC at 40.0 s

acceptance.window: first absolute 0.10-degC departure after 40 s compared with reactor departure
40 through 90 s cascade IAE divided by direct IAE
40 through 90 s peak absolute deviation below direct PI

abortPredicates: Any required signal is nonfinite, stale, forced, or has invalid quality
Any valve request leaves 0 through 100 percent
Any jacket temperature leaves 45 through 90 degC
Any reactor temperature leaves 60 through 95 degC
Inner-loop availability, authority, or restoration is lost
safety.restorationMode: Return utility disturbance to zero and jacket test setpoint to 70 degC; keep the outer controllers tracking until jacket temperatures and valve requests are restored.
safety.physicalApprovalRole: authorised reactor controls engineer and responsible process operator
simulationOnlyRestrictions: No physical reactor is excited or commissioned
Equivalent simulated plants do not prove physical sensor placement or time-scale separation
Physical cascade commissioning requires reviewed topology, interlocks, limits, operating permission and explicit action approval

video.viewerOutcome: Commission an inner jacket loop before closing a reactor outer loop and explain when measured cascade evidence justifies the added structure.

learning.context: Three equivalent jacketed reactors expose the fast jacket state, slow product state, one heating valve and the same bounded utility disturbance.
learning.reason: The preceding feedforward lesson required a measured external disturbance and path model; here the useful early signal is a faster controlled variable through which the disturbance propagates.
theory: The outer reactor loop requests a jacket temperature and never writes the valve directly; the inner jacket loop alone owns valve authority.
The jacket energy balance responds in 2 s while the reactor product balance responds in 12 s, but measured closed-loop settling proves whether the commissioned separation is adequate.
Tracking and constraint propagation prevent inactive or saturated loops from accumulating an unachievable demand.
learning.workedPrediction: A 5-degC jacket-setpoint step exposes the fast and intentionally slow inner tunings; a -10-degC utility event moves jacket temperature before reactor temperature, allowing the fast inner loop to act first.
practicalPreparation: Verify Simulation evidence, the three plant and five controller identities, units, quality, 0.1-s timing, operating point, limits, modes and authority.
Define settling, disturbance-detection lead, reactor event IAE, peak deviation and applied-valve movement before viewing results.
learning.baseline: Run direct reactor-temperature PI through the utility event and retain the response it cannot begin correcting until primary error appears.
learning.change: Commission the two jacket loops first, reject the deliberately slow one, then close the qualified fast inner loop beneath the same outer tuning.
learning.comparison: Hold plant physics, state, disturbance, timing, limits, outer tuning, duration and measure windows equal while changing only structure or inner tuning.
learning.validation: Require a finite bounded fast inner response, at least three-times separation, earlier jacket detection, less than 70 percent of direct reactor IAE and lower peak deviation.
learning.explanation: Cascade improves this plant because the inner jacket sensor observes and corrects utility loss before the slow product temperature moves; merely nesting a slow controller does not create that advantage.
learning.transfer: Use cascade for a faster controllable intermediate variable; the next lesson uses ratio control when product quality instead depends on maintaining a proportion between two measured flows.
